items.s: The storm knocked down our treehouse, so we had to ___ it.
items.tip: re- means 'again': rebuild = build again.
items.say: The storm knocked down our treehouse, so we had to rebuild it.
items.ask: The storm knocked down our treehouse, so we had to blank it.

items.s: Sorry, I ___ the question. Can you say it again?
items.tip: mis- means 'wrongly': misunderstand. In the past: misunderstood.
items.say: Sorry, I misunderstood the question. Can you say it again?
items.ask: Sorry, I blank the question. Can you say it again?

items.s: I ___ and missed the school bus!
items.tip: over- means 'too much': oversleep. The story is in the past: overslept.
items.say: I overslept and missed the school bus!
items.ask: I blank and missed the school bus!

items.s: Leaving your bike unlocked is ___.
items.tip: Words starting with r take ir- for 'not': irresponsible.
items.say: Leaving your bike unlocked is irresponsible.
items.ask: Leaving your bike unlocked is blank.

items.s: In many countries it is ___ to ride a bike at night without lights.
items.tip: Words starting with l take il- for 'not': illegal.
items.say: In many countries it is illegal to ride a bike at night without lights.
items.ask: In many countries it is blank to ride a bike at night without lights.

items.s: Your answer is ___. Have another try!
items.tip: in- means 'not' with many words: incorrect.
items.say: Your answer is incorrect. Have another try!
items.ask: Your answer is blank. Have another try!

items.s: 'Go' is an ___ verb: go, went, gone.
items.tip: regular starts with r, so 'not regular' is irregular.
items.say: 'Go' is an irregular verb: go, went, gone.
items.ask: 'Go' is an blank verb: go, went, gone.

items.s: I ___ the time, so we got to the cinema far too early.
items.tip: mis- = wrongly: miscalculate. Past tense: miscalculated.
items.say: I miscalculated the time, so we got to the cinema far too early.
items.ask: I blank the time, so we got to the cinema far too early.

items.s: The class gave a wonderful ___ of the play.
items.tip: a + adjective + noun: perform + -ance = performance.
items.say: The class gave a wonderful performance of the play.
items.ask: The class gave a wonderful blank of the play.

items.s: Jigsaw puzzles need a lot of ___.
items.tip: a lot of + noun: patient → patience (-ent becomes -ence).
items.say: Jigsaw puzzles need a lot of patience.
items.ask: Jigsaw puzzles need a lot of blank.

items.s: Their ___ started on the first day of school.
items.tip: -ship makes a noun for a relationship: friend → friendship.
items.say: Their friendship started on the first day of school.
items.ask: Their blank started on the first day of school.

items.s: Grandpa told us stories about his ___ on a farm.
items.tip: -hood = the time of being something: childhood = the time when you are a child.
items.say: Grandpa told us stories about his childhood on a farm.
items.ask: Grandpa told us stories about his blank on a farm.

items.s: Swimming is my favourite ___.
items.tip: my favourite + noun: active → activity (drop the e, add -ity).
items.say: Swimming is my favourite activity.
items.ask: Swimming is my favourite blank.

items.s: Our cat's ___ got her stuck in a box again.
items.tip: Adjectives in -ous often make nouns in -osity: curious → curiosity.
items.say: Our cat's curiosity got her stuck in a box again.
items.ask: Our cat's blank got her stuck in a box again.

items.s: Leo has an amazing ___ to remember numbers.
items.tip: an + adjective + noun: able → ability.
items.say: Leo has an amazing ability to remember numbers.
items.ask: Leo has an amazing blank to remember numbers.

items.s: The ___ of the baby panda at the zoo made everyone happy.
items.tip: the … of = a noun: arrive → arrival (drop the e, add -al).
items.say: The arrival of the baby panda at the zoo made everyone happy.
items.ask: The blank of the baby panda at the zoo made everyone happy.

items.s: Lucy is very ___. She is always drawing and making things.
items.tip: very + adjective: create → creative (drop the e, add -ive).
items.say: Lucy is very creative. She is always drawing and making things.
items.ask: Lucy is very blank. She is always drawing and making things.

items.s: We only use ___ ingredients in our cookies.
items.tip: An adjective before a noun: nature → natural.
items.say: We only use natural ingredients in our cookies.
items.ask: We only use blank ingredients in our cookies.

items.s: My uncle is very ___. He has climbed lots of mountains.
items.tip: adventure → adventurous (drop the e, add -ous).
items.say: My uncle is very adventurous. He has climbed lots of mountains.
items.ask: My uncle is very blank. He has climbed lots of mountains.

items.s: Our class did a ___ experiment with vinegar and baking soda.
items.tip: An adjective before experiment: science → scientific.
items.say: Our class did a scientific experiment with vinegar and baking soda.
items.ask: Our class did a blank experiment with vinegar and baking soda.

items.s: The puppy is so ___! He runs around all day.
items.tip: so + adjective: energy → energetic.
items.say: The puppy is so energetic! He runs around all day.
items.ask: The puppy is so blank! He runs around all day.

items.s: We ate ___ food at the Chinese New Year festival.
items.tip: An adjective before food: tradition + -al = traditional.
items.say: We ate traditional food at the Chinese New Year festival.
items.ask: We ate blank food at the Chinese New Year festival.

items.s: A ___ noise came from the attic.
items.tip: mystery + -ous: y changes to i: mysterious.
items.say: A mysterious noise came from the attic.
items.ask: A blank noise came from the attic.

items.s: This video game is too ___. I can't buy it with my pocket money.
items.tip: too + adjective: expense → expensive.
items.say: This video game is too expensive. I can't buy it with my pocket money.
items.ask: This video game is too blank. I can't buy it with my pocket money.
